title: The multiples of 100
keyIdea: Multiples of 100 (100–900) are whole hundreds: a hundreds digit with 0 tens and 0 ones. 300 means 3 hundreds, not 3 tens.
familyTip: Build 300 with three hundred flats. Ask: 'Any tens or ones left?' Compare 400 and 40 on paper.

visual.caption: Multiple of 100 — fair idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build flats, chart hundreds, mark 700, compare 400 vs 40, then challenge.

kid: A multiple of 100 is made of whole hundreds only.
300 means 3 hundreds, 0 tens, and 0 ones — it ends with two zeros.
400 is much more than 40 because the 4 sits in the hundreds place, not the tens place.
On a line to 1000, multiples of 100 sit on the big marks: 100, 200, 300…
adult: CCSS 2.NBT.1.b / NC Y2: 100–900 as amounts of hundreds with empty tens and ones. Words: hundred, multiple, place value, digit.
Common mistakes: reading 400 as 4 tens; writing 5 hundreds as 50; thinking extra zeros are only for looks; placing 700 near 70 on a 0–1000 line.
In the lab your child builds flats, fills a hundreds-tens-ones chart, marks the line, compares 400 vs 40, and chooses 500 for five hundreds.

practice.hint: Whole hundreds only — empty tens and ones.

pool.hint: Tens place is empty in a multiple of 100.
